code-desktop.purpose: The live code; always the largest element. Fluid 24-34px on phones, 38px tablet, 46px desktop.

code-8-desktop.purpose: One step smaller than the 6-digit code so rows keep their width.

issuer.purpose: Service name in a row; 22/19/17px by breakpoint.

body.purpose: Descriptions, notices, form copy, 15px with 1.6 line height.

label.purpose: Column headers, field labels, account names, 14px.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: Flat system. Depth is tone steps plus a 1px ring (ring-1 ring-foreground/10) on menus and popovers; the dialog sits on a 55% black scrim with no blur.

motion.name: hand-tick
motion.purpose: Clock hand angle updated from CodeResult.elapsed via SVG transform attribute; no CSS transition.

motion.name: primitive-fade
motion.purpose: Short fades on menus, dialogs and sheets from the shadcn primitives.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all animation and transition.

narrative.overview:
A code is a departure. The vault reads like a Swiss station timetable: strict columns, black type on an off-white ground, one red that means "act now". Rotation is shown by a station-clock sweep hand per row, never a spinner or a progress ring. Every screen is an Operate surface: the person is usually mid-login elsewhere and needs one correct code in about a second, so the world only lends type, palette, density and the clock; navigation and controls are the standard web ones (shadcn/ui on Radix).

Mobile-first. Designed at 390px, verified at 320px (no horizontal scroll) and widened to strict columns from 768px. Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme` only; there is no theme switch.
keyCharacteristics: Largest element is always the code
One red, spent on action, expiry and the clock hand
Flat: tone steps and 1px rings, no shadows
Light and dark via prefers-color-scheme only

rules.name: The Departure Board Rule
rules.body: The code is always the largest thing on screen. Nothing else in a row may compete with it in size or weight.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red is spent on exactly three things: the primary action, the expiring state, and the clock hand. Errors use the text red because they are a state, not decoration. No red borders, red headings, red icons or red badges anywhere else.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every red state is paired with text: the seconds remaining are always printed ("4 s"), and errors are written sentences.

rules.name: The Grouped Digits Rule
rules.body: Codes are shown grouped ("482 913", "4829 1305") from `CodeResult.formatted`, never as one run. Screen readers get the digits spaced one by one ("4 8 2 9 1 3").

rules.name: The Tone Step Rule
rules.body: If something needs to read as "above", give it the next tone and a 1px ring, never a shadow.

dos: Do keep the code the largest, boldest element in any view that shows one.
Do print seconds remaining as text next to every clock.
Do use tabular figures for anything numeric that updates or aligns.
Do keep 44px minimum targets and 16px input text.
donts: Don't use red for anything except the primary action, the expiring state and the clock hand (plus text-red for errors).
Don't add shadows, blur, gradients, rounded cards or nested containers. Rows are the container.
Don't add a second moving element or animate the hand with CSS transitions.
Don't use inline `style` attributes or `<style>` tags; the CSP blocks them. Use classes and SVG presentation attributes.
Don't add eyebrows or marketing copy. Headings say what the screen is for; errors say what happened and what to do.
